newsitem.title: GREECE: INDUSTRY IS NO MORE THE LOCOMOTIVE OF GREEK ECON - SURVEY.
newsitem.headline: INDUSTRY IS NO MORE THE LOCOMOTIVE OF GREEK ECON - SURVEY.

text.p: The Greek industry is no longer the locomotive of the economy contributing just 13.9 percent to the country's 1995 GDP, said Robert Mc Donald of the EIB and the Greek Industrial Review in a survey of the Greek industry.

The roots of the decline of the Greek industry which accounted for 46.5 percent of export revenues in 1995 can be found in the 1970s but mushroomed in the 1980s when de-industrialisation and troubled firms became household names, the survey showed.
The conclusions of the survey were presented on Monday in a symposium organised by the Athens Chamber of Commerse and Industry and the industrial Review magazine.

The president of the Association of Greek Industrialists (SEV), Iason Stratos was optimistic saying that the share of Greek industry to GDP could climb to 25 percent of GDP by exploiting comparative advantages in agriculture, minerals and lumber.

Yannis Manolis, vice-president at the Confederation of Greek Workers (GSEE), claimed that Greek industry workers were more productive than figures showed because the latter did not take into account the out of date equipment they worked with.

Takis Politis, alternate director of the private Economic and Industrial Research Foundation (IOBE), put it bluntly: "Privatisation or closing down. The majority of industries must close down but we are not ready to accept the shock of unemployment and we perpetuate a situation that creates more unemployment." --Dimitris Kontogiannis, Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4
